title: Governance Polls cannot change anything yet determine what the Executive Vote may contain
content:
A.1.11.1.2.1 defines a Weekly Poll as "a non-binding poll that determines the bi-weekly Executive Vote contents," and clarifies the apparent contradiction: "a weekly poll cannot change the system parameters independently; it merely dictates what will be included in the next Executive Vote."

The combination is the interesting part. The Poll has no executive force at all, yet it functions as an agenda gate — and per A.1.11.1.2.2 an Executive Vote's "contents are often determined by weekly Governance Polls that pre-approve the inclusion of proposals," with direct-to-Executive routes existing only where "the Atlas can explicitly authorize" them.

Splitting sentiment from execution buys two things. Polls can be cheap, numerous and concurrent — A.1.11.1.2.1 notes they "often run concurrently," with formats varying by topic (Binary, Instant Run-Off, Approval) and periods commonly of three or fourteen days — because no single one of them can move the protocol. Meanwhile the on-chain change is concentrated in a bundled, heavily reviewed Executive roughly every two weeks.

The non-obvious consequence is where the real veto sits. Anything that never clears a Poll never reaches an Executive, so a mechanism with no binding power decides most outcomes, while the binding vote is largely ratifying a set already filtered upstream.
description: A Poll is explicitly non-binding — it cannot alter system parameters — but it dictates the contents of the bi-weekly Executive, making it a gate rather than a decision.
